newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Amplats profits seen down on prices, strike.
newsitem.headline: Amplats profits seen down on prices, strike.

text.p: Anglo American Platinum Corp Ltd (Amplats) is set to report reduced earnings next week. A recent rally in Platinum Group Metals prices could have come too late to salvage the company's results, analysts said on Friday.
Amplats, the world's largest platinum producer, is due to report results for the year ended June 30, 1997 on Tuesday.

Analysts said a three-month rally in PGM prices came too late to have any significant impact on Amplats' earnings. To make matters worse, a strike at Rustenburg Platinum Holdings Ltd (Rusplats) in May would also affect earnings.
"The biggest contributing factor is the strike at Rustenburg," BOE Natwest analyst Paul Brogan said.
Analysts polled by Reuters forecast earnings per share for the year in a range of 165.0-186.0 cents, with consensus at 174.0 cents, compared with 190.3 the previous year.
They predicted a dividend of 122.5 cents/share from last year's 120.0 cents, with a range of 120.0-125.0 cents.
Analysts said income from the company's diamond interests could go some way to salvaging the results.
"I think the Amplats results could be bolstered from the diamonds which they may or may not want to show," one analyst said.

"It should be good from the diamonds but they might not show it all because they obviously don't want to make the investor feel that the diamond interests were undervalued in the restructuring," he added.
Amplats said in April it was merging its three mines and the group into one listed company, using Rustenburg as the vehicle.
It said it would also dispose of its diamond interests to De Beers Consolidated Mines Ltd and Anglo American Corp of South Africa Ltd for around 1.2 billion rand ($260.4 million).
Amplats said the restructuring -- due to take place around September -- would allow it to focus on its core business of mining and marketing PGM metals, while helping it to move down the cost curve.

The company said in February it expected full-year earnings to be down on the previous year since dollar prices for platinum, palladium and rhodium had fallen markedly compared with the previous financial year.
Rustenburg was seen reporting earnings of 190.0-235.0 cents per share from last year's 314.4 cents

Earnings at Potgietersrust Platinums Ltd were seen at 97.0-100.0 cents per share from 116.2 cents previously and Lebowa Platinums Ltd was seen earning 1.0-5.5 cents per share from 5.5 the previous year.
